Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Minimal-basis H2: RHF, broken-spin UHF and finite-basis FCI Compare RHF, broken-spin UHF and finite-basis FCI for H2 at two fixed geometries in the same minimal basis. Assumptions, units and boundaries Explicit unchanged STO-3G s contraction, R1.4/3.0bohr, finite-basis FCI and broken-spin UHF; not exact continuum chemistry. Distances1.4/3.0bohr and total energies in hartree. Two electrons in2AOs, each an explicitly supplied three-primitive contracted Hs function. Editorial clarification Only2fixed distances. Finite-basis FCI is not continuum exactness, and UHF stationarity is not a general global-minimum guarantee. Angular/complete-basis convergence and a broad dissociation curve remain untested. Adopted numerical method Run fixed SCF and diagonalize the4x4 two-electron Hamiltonian using the unchanged explicit H STO-3G contraction. Verification limits and failures Only two H2 geometries and two contracted s orbitals; no complete-basis dissociation curve. UHF is spin contaminated; FCI exactness is finite-basis only.
